title: The Call Desk
subtitle: Claude vs. the networks · election night 2026

rule.headline: A race is called only at 99.5% confidence or more.
rule.text: Senate and governor polling averages have historically missed by about five points on average, so a 99.5% (2.6σ) call on polls alone needs a lead of 13 points or more. None of these ten races has one, so the first calls will come from the returns: a race is called when the outstanding vote, at any plausible composition, cannot close the gap. Nothing is called before a state's polls close. Every call carries its timestamp; a wrong call is withdrawn in public and stays in the log. Races with no public polling (House seats, down-ballot offices) can be called at poll close only when every rater has them Solid or Safe and the district voted for the 2024 presidential winner by 20 points or more under the current map; everything else waits for the count.
rule.scoring: Scored against the Associated Press: a call counts when AP later calls the same winner. The AP column shows AP's own call and time as recorded by the Election Desk.

races.name: Georgia Senate
races.note: A 9-point lead is short of the 13 the rule needs. Georgia counts its early vote first, so the first drops will run Democratic; the test is the Election Day vote in the Atlanta exurbs. A majority is required, or it goes to a December runoff.

races.name: Georgia Governor

pollAvg.src: Election Desk mean of 5 polls, Oct. 12–Nov. 2

races.note: The closest race on the board: Research Co. had Bottoms +1, InsiderAdvantage a tie. A runoff is live if nobody clears 50%.

races.name: South Carolina Senate

pollAvg.src: Election Desk mean of 7 polls; PollCheck final average Graham +1.1

races.note: A state Trump carried by 18. If Andrews is within a few points as the Upstate reports, the polls were right and this goes late.

races.name: Ohio Senate (special)

pollAvg.src: Poliwave average, Nov. 1; RealClearPolling has Husted +1

races.note: The averages disagree most here. Ohio reports early and absentee first; watch the margin in Franklin, Cuyahoga and Hamilton against 2024, then the Election Day vote in the rest of the state.

races.name: North Carolina Senate
races.note: Closest to the 13-point line. North Carolina's early vote reports within minutes of 7:30; if Cooper's early-vote margin matches the polls this can be called early.

races.name: Maine Senate

pollAvg.src: Poliwave average, Nov. 2; Silver Bulletin D +3.9

races.note: Collins has beaten her polls before. Maine counts by town and slowly; ranked-choice tabulation only if nobody reaches 50%.

races.name: Texas Senate

pollAvg.src: Poliwave average, Nov. 2; Silver Bulletin D +3.3

races.note: Texas reports its early vote in one large drop around 8 p.m. ET; Election Day votes follow county by county. Most of the state closes at 8, El Paso at 9.

races.name: Michigan Senate
races.note: Michigan now pre-processes mail ballots, so the count is faster than 2020. Wayne and Oakland are the keys; the Upper Peninsula closes at 9.

races.name: Iowa Senate

pollAvg.src: Poliwave average, Nov. 1; Silver Bulletin D +1.1

races.note: A coin flip in the polls. Iowa counts fast; the call will come from the full count, not a projection.

races.name: Kansas Senate
races.note: No Democrat has won a Kansas Senate race since 1932. Johnson County (Kansas City suburbs) decides it; the rural vote reports late.

races.name: Kentucky 6th District

pollAvg.src: Mean of three Oct. polls (Change Research 47–38, DCCC 46–40, GQR 42–37), all Democratic-sponsored; no nonpartisan public poll

lean.src: 2024 presidential vote in the district (Election Desk)
lean.ratings: Cook Toss-up · Sabato Lean R · Inside Tilt R

races.note: Open seat (Barr left to run for Senate). Polls closed at 6 p.m. ET. Every public poll is Democratic-sponsored, so the desk discounts the lead; a Trump +15 district needs the count. Fayette County (Lexington) reports first and will run Dembo; the test is the rural counties.

races.name: Ohio Governor

pollAvg.src: Election Desk mean of 11 polls, Oct. 12–Nov. 2 (NYT/Siena 49–43, Atlas 52–44, Emerson 48–48)

races.note: Open seat; DeWine is term-limited. Same early-vote-first count as the Senate race: watch the three big counties, then the Election Day vote.

races.name: Ohio Attorney General

lean.src: 2022 attorney general result (Yost 59–41); no public polling
lean.ratings: Not rated; Faber is the sitting auditor

races.note: Open seat; Yost is term-limited. Down-ballot Republicans won every Ohio statewide office by about 20 in 2022; the question is how much of a D+8 national year reaches this line.

lean.ratings: Not rated; Sprague is the sitting treasurer

races.note: Open seat; LaRose is term-limited and running for auditor. Russo is the Ohio House minority leader.

races.name: Ohio Supreme Court: Brunner seat

lean.src: Republicans won the three 2024 Ohio Supreme Court seats by 10–14 points; no public polling

races.note: Party labels have been on the ballot for court seats since 2022. Brunner is the last Democrat on the seven-member court.

races.name: Ohio Supreme Court: Zayas v. Hawkins

log.text: 6:03 p.m. ET: Board set. Ten races, calls so far: 0. Nothing has closed, and none of the ten clears a 99.5% bar on polling alone. First results check at 7:40 p.m., then hourly.

6:45 p.m. ET: Added Kentucky's 6th District and every Ohio race on the ballot: governor, attorney general, secretary of state, auditor, treasurer, two Supreme Court seats and all 15 U.S. House districts. Eight Ohio House seats (2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 11, 12, 14) are callable at 7:30 under the no-polling rule; everything else waits for the count.

7:03 p.m. ET: Check #1 (run early). Georgia and South Carolina closed at 7; nothing counted yet in the board's races, Kentucky's 6th still at 0% on DDHQ. No calls. Ohio closes at 7:30; the eight at-close Ohio House seats are called on the 7:40 check.
